maya_support: Hey team — customer seeing intermittent 429 bursts for our embeddings endpoint. Happens around spikes, but sometimes with the same API key. Example header from a failing request: `x-request-id: req_8a7f9c2b` and response: `429 Too Many Requests`.

maya_support: Quick curl that hit it:
```bash
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY' \n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  -d '{"input": ["test"], "model": "open-embed-3-small"}'
```

alex_dev: Thanks — can you paste minimal repro snippets for Python/JS/Go so engs can run locally? Also include env + header capture. :eyes:

maya_support: Yep — sharing tiny repros. Each prints response status + headers + body, and logs `x-request-id` if present.

maya_support: Python (requests):
```python
import os
import requests

API_KEY = os.getenv("REDWOOD_API_KEY")
url = "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings"
headers = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {API_KEY}", "Content-Type": "application/json"}
json = {"input": ["test"], "model": "open-embed-3-small"}
resp = requests.post(url, headers=headers, json=json, timeout=10)
print(resp.status_code)
print(dict(resp.headers))
print(resp.text)
if resp.headers.get('x-request-id'):
    print('REQID=', resp.headers['x-request-id'])
```

maya_support: Node (fetch):
```javascript
const fetch = require('node-fetch');
const API_KEY = process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY;
(async () => {
  const res = await fetch('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings', {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: { 'Authorization': `Bearer ${API_KEY}`, 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
    body: JSON.stringify({ input: ['test'], model: 'open-embed-3-small' }),
  });
  console.log(res.status);
  console.log(Object.fromEntries(res.headers.entries()));
  console.log(await res.text());
})();
```

maya_support: Go (net/http):
```go
package main

import (
  "bytes"
  "fmt"
  "io/ioutil"
  "net/http"
  "os"
)

func main() {
  apiKey := os.Getenv("REDWOOD_API_KEY")
  body := []byte(`{"input":["test"],"model":"open-embed-3-small"}`)
  req, _ := http.NewRequest("POST", "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings", bytes.NewBuffer(body))
  req.Header.Set("Authorization", "Bearer "+apiKey)
  req.Header.Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
  client := &http.Client{}
  resp, err := client.Do(req)
  if err != nil { panic(err) }
  defer resp.Body.Close()
  b, _ := ioutil.ReadAll(resp.Body)
  fmt.Println(resp.StatusCode)
  fmt.Println(resp.Header)
  fmt.Println(string(b))
}
```

ingrid_se: Nice, can we add instructions to enable debug headers and capture server trace? Suggest asking the user to set `REDWOOD_DEBUG=1` and rerun so the system returns extra trace headers. Also request the full `x-request-id` plus `date` and `via` headers if present.

alex_dev: If they can run these and paste the captured headers + the printed req id we can correlate with infra logs. Also ask them to run the python snippet with an aggressive retry disabled (no automatic retry) so we see raw 429s.

support-bot: Tip: To collect a debug bundle run with `REDWOOD_DEBUG=1` and include the three most recent `x-request-id`s plus the approximate wall time (UTC). Use `--diag` in our CLI to bundle logs.

maya_support: Will ask customer to run now. I'll request: 3 failing req ids, full response headers, small local timestamps, and whether they're behind a proxy (corporate NAT). Will post results back here. :thumbsup:

alex_dev: Great — once we have that, eng will run quick grep across the 429 window and share probable rate-limiter/ingestion hints.

maya_support: FYI posted follow-up in the thread when customer runs. Thanks all.
